author: haiku
label: c2-nat-haiku-01
changes: Removed the 'version' condition on the breach streak and the version column. Each tick's writes now run in one transaction that checks the tick claim is still held, then marks the tick done. This is the guard against a re-run double-counting.
Made the incident insert, level-1 page row, level-2 job, send job and tick-done mark one transaction, so a crash cannot leave a partial state.
Moved provider sends out of the evaluator path into a queued send job that runs after commit, with retries and status on the page row.
Fixed the diagram so an incident-insert conflict records the breach on the existing incident and stops, with no page.
Added the missed-tick branch (metrics query failed) to the diagram, matching the rule notes.
Added the breach-on-open-incident clean-streak reset to the diagram, which was missing.
Added the claim lease takeover and tick granularity (one tick per service and rule pair, minute from the store clock).
Added the ack webhook steps: signature check, page-ID lookup, idempotent set, and cancel queued escalations.
Made the escalation job re-read the incident and check ack status in the same transaction as its inserts, so an ack cannot slip in between.
Stated that the job queue lives in the same database, so enqueueing commits with the rows.
Added a delivery row to the failure table saying the system does not track delivery.
Noted in open questions that the provider's page ID timing and delivery receipts are unknown.
Moved the breach and clean streaks off the incidents table onto a new rule_state row per service and rule, so the streak exists before any incident does (Q10).
Added Window and Rule state to Terms, and stated that consecutive ticks overlap by four minutes (Q11).
Changed the tick-claim takeover and fence description so the fence is one conditional update first in the transaction, and a lost claim writes nothing (Q16).
Changed the diagram's second-instance exit to cover an already-done tick, and the send-job note to cover resolved notices (Q14, Q16).
Explained cancel of queued escalations in the delayed job queue bullet, and that level 3 is queued only by a successful level-2 page (Q12).
Added a Sending pages section covering the send job's inputs, provider page ID, retry scope, stop conditions and resolved notices (Q13, Q14, Q17).
Moved the roster to rule_state, defined its contents and when it is written, and changed the schedule-down row to use the roster slot for the level being paged (Q15).
Added an open question on the retry limit and backoff schedule, since the brief sets none (Q17).

Tick flow: each wake now tries the pair's current tick and the one before it, earlier first, and a tick waits until the same pair's previous tick is done. This fixes a tick being lost when its holder dies, and keeps streaks in order.
Clean-streak resolution moved into the same fenced transaction as the clean-streak increment and tick-done mark. Both streaks are set to 0 on resolve.
Opening an incident sets the breach streak to 0. The clean streak is kept at 0 while no incident is open. This was implicit before and is now stated.

Diagram: every tick branch is labelled as a fenced transaction. Percent signs and semicolons were replaced with words so the Mermaid parses cleanly. The ack webhook branch for an unknown page ID is added.
Empty roster at open: the incident still opens, the level-1 page row has no person, a failure alarm is raised, and the level-2 job is queued as normal.
Escalation and ack both lock the incident row, so an ack and a level-2 page cannot interleave. An ack that lands after a level-2 commit cancels the level-3 job.
Level 3 is now queued in the same transaction as the level-2 page row, even when no person was found. This replaces the earlier 'only a successful level-2 page' wording.
Send job: stated as at-least-once. A duplicate push after a crash before the page ID is stored is accepted and added to the failure table and open questions.
Sending pages: the stop rules for page retries and for resolved-notice retries are now stated separately.
Ack: any level's page ID finds its incident, any ack stops escalation, and acked_by is the person on the acked page.

Structure: summary, terms, diagram, numbered steps, state, coordination, sending, rules, one failure table, open questions. Failure handling is no longer repeated across notes, and the Q-style codes are gone.
Terms: added between, low volume, fenced transaction, roster and tick claim lease. Removed nothing the brief or the first version stated.
Step 1: stated when a tick that waits on an earlier tick runs (same wake if this instance won the earlier tick, else next wake) and that the 30-second lease is set at claim (Q25).
Step 3: stated that the streaks are read from rule_state before deciding and re-read inside the fenced transaction, which writes from that read (Q26).
Step 5 and Rules to confirm: stated that page rows and ack fields stay as recorded on resolve, and that a later breach opens a new incident with streaks from 0 (Q29).
Sending pages and the failure table: a page with no person sends nothing and is not retried, and a resolved notice is handled the same way (Q27).
Where state lives: added the jobs table and a job worker that runs inside each evaluator process, with duplicate runs made harmless by the row lock and unique level (Q28).
Sending pages: a page keeps one provider page ID normally, with the crash case stated as the only route to a second push (Q30).
Opening facts moved into the failure table as one row, and the outside-transactions fact kept only under coordination, so each fact appears once.
Terms: added Provider, Webhook, Row lock, Job queue worker wording and Store clock, so the newcomer terms are defined in one line each.
Open questions: added the SMS page ID gap (push fails, SMS used, no ID stored) and the one-tick look-back stall found while answering Q25.

Put the diagram directly after the summary and terms, as the skill's diagram form requires. The steps are now notes after it. Each step names its trigger, the data it keeps and its rules. Failures are not repeated inside the steps.
Added a three-sentence summary. It says how the cron email works today and how paging replaces it.

Added a one-line definition for every new term, including evaluator, complete minute, fenced transaction, partial unique index, idempotent, signature, backoff, dead-man heartbeat and send job. Dropped the definitions of transaction and row lock, which are everyday terms.

Merged the separate Rule interpretations and Rules to confirm sections into the steps and the state section where each applies: low volume, between, streak resets on open and resolve, missed ticks, ack not changing status, and fresh level 1 for a new incident.
Merged Sending pages into step 7 (Send) and kept every rule in it. These include the person chosen at page time, no-person pages, resolved notices, the at-least-once delivery and the single push ID.
Merged Coordination and Duplicate suppression into one section and removed the repeated takeover and lost-lease text. Each guard is stated once.

Failure table: kept every row from the first version and from the Q&A. Added rows for the earlier-tick holder crash, the job worker crash and the duplicate ack's idempotent handler. Combined the two schedule-lookup rows into one.

Added the Q&A clarifications into the steps: a failed lookup at open still opens the incident; level 3 is queued only by a successful level-2 commit; the roster is written only when the lookup succeeded.
Kept the diagram from the last version. Its content is unchanged except that the fenced-transaction labels and the ack and resolution branches already match the steps. No design decision was changed.
Kept all seven open questions, reworded to be self-contained.
